Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Singleton
Analyst: Peter Grogan
Date: 01/31/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 59 as introduced establishes the Prison PREP Pilot Program for Small Business Development for Ex-Offenders, under the Board of Pardons and Paroles (Board) and the Department of Corrections (DOC) effective July 1, 2022 through December 31, 2027, subject to the availability of funds. This would increase the obligations of the Board and the DOC, by an undetermined amount to: 1) establish training locations and funding for participants to receive training on establishment of small businesses; 2) provide assistance in obtaining small business funding; 3) partner with entities to provide mentorship to individuals for three years; and 4) to provide an annual report on the effectiveness of the program to the Legislature and the Legislative Services Agency by the fifth legislative day of each regular session.
For fiscal year 2022, DOC was appropriated $200,000 and the Board was appropriated $125,000 from the State General Fund. The fiscal year 2023 Governor recommended General Fund Budget appropriates $200,000 to DOC and $125,000 to the Board.
This bill could further increase the obligations of J. F. Ingram State Community College, paid from the Education Trust Fund, by an undetermined amount, to provide training in small business development to inmates exiting the correctional system.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Senate Bill 59 as passed the Senate establishes the Prison PREP Pilot Program for Small Business Development for Ex-Offenders, under the Board of Pardons and Paroles (Board) and the Department of Corrections (DOC) effective July 1, 2022 through December 31, 2027, subject to the availability of funds. This would increase the obligations of the Board and the DOC, by an undetermined amount to: 1) establish training locations and funding for participants to receive training on establishment of small businesses; 2) provide assistance in obtaining small business funding; 3) partner with entities to provide mentorship to individuals for three years; and 4) to provide an annual report on the effectiveness of the program to the Legislature and the Legislative Services Agency by the fifth legislative day of each regular session.

The fiscal year 2023 Governor Recommended General Fund Appropriation bill includes a $200,000 appropriation to DOC and $125,000 appropriation to the Board.
This bill could further increase the obligations of J. F. Ingram State Community College, paid from the Education Trust Fund, by an undetermined amount, to provide training in small business development to inmates exiting the correctional system.
Steve Clouse, Chair
